data.title: What's driving SanDisk stock higher today?
data.description:
SanDisk (SNDK) shares are pushing higher on Friday after its flash manufacturing partner, Kioxia, showed how solid-state drives could help Nvidia’s AI systems work with much larger datasets.

The November 27 rebound followed a 5.6% drop on Wednesday – which was the last US trading session before Thanksgiving.

What caught investors’ attention was the prospect that AI servers could use more NAND flash to process data, adding another source of demand for the chips SanDisk makes.

SanDisk stock is currently down more than 70% versus its year-to-date high.

Here’s what is behind SanDisk stock’s surge

Kioxia equipped an Nvidia GB200 NVL72 rack with 144 NVMe solid-state drives (SSDs), giving it roughly 1.1 petabytes of raw flash capacity.

Nvidia’s software lets GPUs tap that extra capacity when a dataset is too large to fit in their high-bandwidth memory.

Kioxia estimates the setup could handle up to 2 trillion vectors, numerical representations that AI systems use to find related information.

For SanDisk, the potential opportunity lies in how much NAND flash AI infrastructure could require as workloads grow.

The company shares manufacturing joint ventures with Kioxia, whose agreements run through 2034.

However, the Nvidia demonstration does not establish additional orders for SanDisk.

A broader adoption of SSD-based memory expansion could create another source of NAND demand, but the commercial implications will depend on future deployments and supply agreements.

SNDK shares could rebound sharply in 2027

At Friday’s early price, SanDisk shares were still roughly 42% below their November 2 close on a “split-adjusted” basis.

Its latest earnings give investors a reason to revisit that selloff.

Data-center sales jumped 61% from the prior quarter to $4.8 billion – and SanDisk expects overall revenue to reach at least $12.2 billion in its fiscal second quarter, up from $11 billion.

Management also said long-term agreements cover about half of its planned flash volume for fiscal 2027 and two-thirds for fiscal 2028.

If those commitments translate into shipments at healthy prices, investors could regain confidence in how much of SanDisk’s recent earnings growth it can sustain.

What to look for moving forward?

Kioxia and Nvidia are still evaluating the technology, so the demonstration’s effect on SanDisk’s sales remains uncertain.

The clearest evidence will come from additional supply agreements with large cloud providers and from how much of SanDisk’s revenue growth comes from shipping more flash.

Management said higher prices accounted for about 40% of the latest quarter’s sequential revenue increase, with higher volumes accounting for the rest.

That matters because weaker NAND prices could blunt the earnings benefit even if data centers buy more drives. A sustained recovery into 2027 would be easier to justify if SanDisk Corp keeps growing shipment volumes while protecting its margins.

Note that Wall Street currently has a consensus “Buy” rating on SNDK stock with a bullish mean price target of nearly $264, indicating massive upside potential from here.

data.title: Micron, SK Hynix, SanDisk stocks rise but what's the verdict on demand outlook?
data.description:
Micron Technology, SK Hynix and SanDisk shares rebounded on Friday as investors returned to technology and artificial intelligence-linked stocks, bringing some relief after a volatile week for the semiconductor sector.

Micron shares MU rose about 1.2% in early trading, while South Korea's SK Hynix gained around 6% and SanDisk advanced nearly 5.3%.

The recovery extended across the AI trade, with Nvidia, Intel and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) all climbing higher at open.

Nasdaq opened over 1.5% higher.

However, Friday's gains came after a steep monthly decline.

Micron has lost more than 35% over the past month, while SK Hynix is down about 24% and SanDisk has fallen 55%.

The recent weakness reflects growing investor anxiety over whether the enormous investment in AI infrastructure will generate sufficient revenue and profits to justify the spending.

Concerns about a Democratic sweep of Congress and the possibility of tighter scrutiny of data centre construction have added to uncertainty around future chip demand.

For memory manufacturers, the central question is whether the current supply shortage and elevated prices can persist as data centre projects face potential delays and customers reconsider how much memory they need.

Analysts warn of mounting memory oversupply risks

BNP Paribas downgraded Micron to Neutral from Outperform earlier this week, warning that the risk of an "oversupply scenario is mounting" in the memory market.

Analyst Karl Ackerman also slashed his price target to $775 from $1,700.

Ackerman expects memory demand to peak earlier than previously anticipated, potentially setting the stage for excess supply as manufacturers bring additional capacity online.

He highlighted permitting delays affecting data centre construction as a significant risk.

The memory and storage industry is "heavily reliant" on data centre projects, with servers accounting for at least half of demand for dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) and NAND flash memory.

If construction is delayed, spending on servers and associated memory could also be postponed.

That would give manufacturers more time to increase supply, potentially narrowing the gap between demand and available capacity.

Another concern is that rising memory prices are prompting technology vendors to reduce the amount of memory used in their products.

Ackerman pointed to Nvidia's decision to reduce high-bandwidth memory content in its new Vera Rubin Ultra architecture, as well as reductions in memory specifications across personal computers and mobile devices.

The consumer market presents an additional challenge because long-term volume and price agreements are uncommon in the PC and mobile segments.

That makes it harder for memory manufacturers to secure favourable pricing and protect margins when demand weakens.

GF Securities cuts 2027 DRAM price forecasts

Fresh concerns emerged on Friday after GF Securities lowered its forecast for DRAM contract prices in 2027, citing order reductions among Chinese customers.

The Hong Kong-based investment firm now expects quarterly contract price increases of 6%, 3%, 0% and 0% across the four quarters of 2027.

Its previous estimates were 10%, 7%, 5% and 3%, respectively.

The revision reflects weaker demand signals from Chinese cloud service providers, according to data from TrendForce.

In a report published on Friday, TrendForce warned that uncertainty surrounding data centre investment could weigh on DRAM demand over the next two years.

Its base-case scenario sees conventional DRAM contract price increases narrowing throughout 2027, with prices potentially stabilising in the second half before declining in 2028.

A more pessimistic scenario suggests prices could begin falling as early as the fourth quarter of 2027 if server manufacturers reduce procurement and inventories.

TrendForce cited lower server DRAM demand from Chinese cloud providers, potential restrictions on data centre development and expanding production capacity among memory manufacturers.

“The shortage of GPU has led to the server DRAM order cut from Chinese CSPs, affecting ~1% of total DRAM demand, which can be absorbed by US [cloud service providers],” GF analysts wrote in a note to clients.

“Besides, consumer DRAM demand is softer due to the order cut of eSSD and spec downgrade of consumer electronics, which will place downward pressure on consumer DRAM pricing, especially for DDR4.”

Supply constraints could support Micron and SK Hynix

Despite the downward revisions, GF Securities does not expect the memory market to move immediately into a prolonged supply glut.

The firm believes DRAM supply could remain tight until 2028, partly because manufacturers are allocating more capacity towards high-bandwidth memory used in AI systems.

That could encourage major suppliers, including Micron, SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics, to remain cautious about expanding conventional memory production.

“If demand weakness persists and prices roll over, the potential production cut is under consideration, which can better support the LTA floor price,” the analysts added.

“We remain constructive on main DRAM vendors including Micron, SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics, as we see the downward revision more limited and potential production cut to maintain price,” the analysts explained.

The contrasting outlooks leave memory investors weighing near-term demand risks against the possibility that disciplined production and continued AI infrastructure spending will keep supply constrained.

Friday's rebound suggests buyers are still willing to return to the sector, but the durability of the recovery will depend on whether memory prices and data centre investment can withstand the emerging headwinds.

data.title: Nasdaq opens 1.5% higher as US equities head for weekly gains despite volatility
data.description:
US stocks opened sharply higher on Friday as investors returned from the Thanksgiving holiday and bought beaten-down technology and artificial intelligence shares.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 507 points, or 1%, at the opening bell. The S&P 500 gained 1.2%, while the Nasdaq Composite jumped 1.5% to kick off a shortened trading day.

All three major benchmarks were headed for strong weekly gains, despite mid-week volatility.

Technology stocks led the advance, with Nvidia rising 3% at the opening bell. Anthropic kicked up 5% in early trading.

AMD, Broadcom and other major AI-linked companies are also sharply recovering some of their recent losses.

The rebound follows a turbulent week on Wall Street, with the Nasdaq 100 briefly touching bear-market territory on Wednesday before recovering.

The week began with a strong rally, with Jensen Huang returning as the CEO of Nvidia. However, the gains soon fizzled as the AI trade continued to unravel.

Concerns about the enormous cost of AI infrastructure, rising borrowing requirements and the ability of companies to generate sufficient returns have weighed on investor sentiment.

"The recovery in stocks seems technical. The questions that caused the market panic are still unanswered," Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB, told Reuters. "If these gains can be sustained on Friday, it would suggest that enthusiasm for the AI trade is back."

"(Investors) felt that the selloff that we saw going into last Friday was overdone. It would be more of a steady push up from here, possibly," said David Morrison, senior market analyst at Trade Nation.

Asian tech stocks lead global recovery

The buying interest was already visible across international markets before Wall Street reopened.

South Korea's Kospi surged 4.3% on Friday, supported by strong gains in semiconductor stocks.

Japan's Nikkei 225 added 2.1%, while China's Shanghai Composite rose 3.7%.

European markets were also trading higher, with the FTSE 100 up around 0.7%.

The global recovery has offered some encouragement to US investors, although the shortened Black Friday trading session could result in relatively thin volumes.

Fed rate hike bets remain a concern

Meanwhile, markets are still contending with the prospect of another Federal Reserve interest rate increase.

Fed funds futures are pricing in approximately 99% odds of a 25-basis-point hike at the December 9-10 meeting, which would take the target range to 4%-4.25%.

Persistent inflation and stronger-than-expected economic growth have strengthened expectations of further monetary tightening, potentially limiting the scope for a sustained stock market recovery.

Torsten Slok, chief economist at Apollo Global Management, believes the market turmoil provides a strong argument for caution.

"If they look at inflation, they should be hiking. But if you look at the outlook for AI, they should maybe be cutting," Slok told the Financial Times.

Oil prices are another concern.

Brent crude was trading around a three-week high in the session before paring some gains to reach $95.88 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate was up over 1% near $84.54.

Prices have gained over several sessions amid attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.

Investors are also assessing the implications of fresh tariff proposals from the Trump administration.

The US has proposed additional duties on imports from 14 trading partners, including China, Japan, India and the European Union, citing concerns over excess industrial capacity.

data.title: Dow futures surge 650 points: 5 things to know before Wall Street opens
data.description:
US stock futures surged on Friday as investors returned from Thanksgiving with renewed appetite for beaten-down technology shares, even as stubborn inflation and fresh tariff proposals threatened the recovery.

Nasdaq 100 futures jumped 2.47%, S&P 500 contracts gained 1.65% and Dow futures rose 1.33%, or 656 points.

The rebound followed Wednesday's volatile session, when the Nasdaq Composite recovered from a drop of more than 4% to close 0.6% lower.

5 things to know before Wall Street opens

1. Black Friday offers a test of consumers and retailer margins

Adobe Analytics forecasts $12.9 billion in US online spending on Friday, up 9.2% from a year earlier, followed by $15.1 billion on Cyber Monday. That would contribute to a record $275.1 billion holiday shopping season.

Shoppers had already spent $82.5 billion online between 1 and 22 November, Adobe estimates. But discounts were 8% deeper than a year earlier, according to Salesforce.

Amazon, Walmart, Target and Best Buy will be judged on margins as well as sales. Higher sales may reflect inflation or bargain hunting, rather than stronger demand.

2. December Fed rate hike bets remain near certainty

Wednesday's data reinforced expectations of further tightening. Headline personal consumption expenditures inflation reached 3.8% in October, while the core measure increased 3.3%, above the Fed's 2% target.

Third-quarter economic growth was revised to an annualised 4.3%, from an initial estimate of 3.4%.

Futures markets assigned roughly 99% probability to a quarter-point December rate increase. The next major test is the 4 December employment report.

Stronger growth supports company profits, but sustained high yields can depress valuations, particularly among technology businesses.

3. Trump's proposed tariffs threaten corporate profit margins

Washington proposed duties on 14 economies, including China, India, Japan and the European Union, following an investigation into manufacturing overcapacity.

The US Trade Representative outlined rates of up to 20% on some Chinese goods and 25% on Indian imports, subject to exemptions and existing duties. EU goods face a proposed 15% rate.

These are proposals, not tariffs already collected. Public comments are due in January.

Retailers, carmakers and industrial companies face uncertainty over input costs, while an increase in import prices could complicate the Fed's inflation fight.

4. Nvidia recovery faces a fresh credit-rating test

Nvidia stock rose before Friday's opening bell after November's steep losses.

However, S&P Global Ratings has placed the chipmaker's AA credit rating on watch for a possible downgrade, pointing to governance and succession concerns following Jensen Huang's reinstatement.

Anthropic has slipped below its IPO price, adding to AI valuation concerns.

Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB, argues the rebound may reflect technical buying rather than resolution of the industry's central questions over spending and returns.

Thin holiday trading could magnify moves in either direction.

5. Oil rebounds as OPEC+ prepares its supply decision

Brent climbed 1.2% to $97.71 a barrel at 07:45 GMT, heading for its first weekly gain in four weeks. WTI stood at $86.27, up 3.1% from Wednesday's settlement because US markets were shut Thursday.

Attacks on shipping and Saudi energy infrastructure are reviving supply concerns ahead of Sunday's OPEC+ meeting. Members may hold output targets through early 2027, although no decision has been announced.

Higher crude could lift US energy shares, but it also risks adding to inflation pressures.

data.title: Adidas, Puma stocks fall as JPMorgan downgrades both on 2027 outlook
data.description:
Adidas and Puma shares fell on Friday after JPMorgan downgraded both German sportswear makers as part of its 2027 sector outlook, citing slowing industry growth, intensifying competition and limited scope for further gains.

Adidas shares were down more than 2%, while Puma declined about 1.7%.

JPMorgan lowered its price target on Adidas by 20% to €184 from €230, with analyst Chiara Battistini cutting the stock's rating from Buy to Neutral.

The revised target implies about 9% upside from Friday's trading levels.

Separately, analyst Wendy Liu downgraded Puma to Underweight from Neutral and reduced the price target to €21 from €26.

Adidas shares are up more than 1% year to date, while Puma has advanced over 5%.

JPMorgan questions Adidas' growth prospects

JPMorgan said it was becoming more difficult to support Adidas's target of high-single-digit sales growth in 2027 without clearer evidence that its major product franchises could expand further.

The brokerage pointed to lifestyle franchise Stan Smith and running lines Hyperboost and Supernova, saying their ability to scale would be important in sustaining growth.

While the firm remains optimistic about Adidas's apparel business, it sees limited scope for additional upside against a challenging comparable base.

Direct-to-consumer sales have been a bright spot, but JPMorgan warned that growth in the channel could become more expensive in the fourth quarter and into 2027 if the company relies increasingly on promotions.

The brokerage also cautioned that Adidas's current targets of high-single-digit revenue growth and a double-digit operating margin in 2027 leave little room for disappointment in a volatile market.

JPMorgan's fiscal 2027 and fiscal 2028 estimates are high-single-digit and double-digit percentages below consensus, respectively.

The downgrade follows Adidas's latest quarterly results last month, which showed net profit rising to €706 million ($787.4 million) for the quarter ended September, from €461 million a year earlier.

The company also confirmed preliminary sales of €7.25 billion and operating profit of €1.01 billion.

JPMorgan had described the results as reassuring, although it flagged weakness in wholesale footwear sales in Europe.

Adidas maintained its upgraded 2026 guidance, which calls for operating profit of around €2.5 billion and currency-neutral revenue growth of between 9% and 10%.

Puma faces tougher market conditions despite inventory progress

JPMorgan's downgrade of Puma reflects concerns about the broader sportswear industry's growth outlook and the company's ability to regain momentum amid intensifying competition.

However, Puma's recent results have offered some encouragement about its restructuring efforts.

The company reported third-quarter sales of €1.77 billion, down 5% year over year but slightly above analysts' average estimate of €1.75 billion.

Inventories declined 24.3% to €1.6 billion, reflecting lower purchasing volumes.

The reduction has reassured investors about Puma's efforts to normalise stock levels and improve its cost structure, as well as its partnership with Chinese retail giant Anta Sports.

UBS analysts said investors should find the results reassuring, as they suggest Puma remains on track to normalise inventory levels by the end of the year despite a challenging market environment.

Puma also narrowed its 2026 operating result guidance to a loss of between €80 million and €130 million, compared with its previous range of a loss of €50 million to €150 million.

However, questions remain about how quickly the company can return to growth.

Deutsche Bank said in a note to clients after the earnings release: "We need to see more confidence on the 2027 and mid-term outlook at some stage."

The latest downgrades suggest that investors may have to look beyond inventory improvements and near-term earnings resilience when assessing the two sportswear companies.

Their ability to sustain sales growth, protect margins and strengthen their product franchises will be critical as the industry heads into 2027.

data.title: Switzerland’s first spot bitcoin ETF debuts on SIX with 350 BTC in assets
data.description:
Switzerland’s first exchange-traded fund to invest directly in bitcoin has begun trading on SIX Swiss Exchange, giving investors in the country a fund-based alternative to the debt-style crypto products that dominate Europe.

The Bitcoin Fund ETF, ticker BBIT, listed on November 26, 2026, SIX said in a media release. Pernet von Ballmoos AG (PvB) is the issuer and fund management company, while BIT Asset Management is sponsor, asset manager and distributor.

BIT Asset Management, the Zurich-based subsidiary of Singapore-headquartered digital asset platform BIT, formerly Matrixport, said the fund launched with 350 bitcoin in assets. The Block put the value of that holding at more than $20 million.

A fund rather than a note

The Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA) approved the fund on October 20, 2026, describing it as the first exchange-traded retail fund in Switzerland to invest directly in bitcoin.

FINMA classified it as an “other fund for alternative investments” with a specific risk under Swiss law. It granted an exemption from the usual risk diversification rules, citing bitcoin’s long trading history and high trading volume.

BIT Asset Management said the approval followed an 18-month review. FINMA added that other fund providers have also submitted or announced applications for bitcoin ETFs.

The distinction matters because most bitcoin products listed in Europe are exchange-traded products (ETPs). These are debt instruments that carry the credit risk of their issuer, BIT noted.

BBIT, by contrast, is a Swiss investment fund governed by the Collective Investment Schemes Act (CISA). Its assets are legally segregated, and investors hold fund units rather than a claim on the issuer.

The fund’s bitcoin is held in segregated cold storage at AMINA Bank, a FINMA-regulated Swiss bank, according to BIT. The fund does not use derivatives or securities lending.

“The economic exposure of a fund and a note can look very similar when everything goes well. The difference is what happens when it doesn’t,” said Friedrich Herzog, chief investment officer of BIT Asset Management.

In the EU, retail funds under UCITS rules generally cannot hold a single crypto asset directly, which has left ETPs as the main listed route to bitcoin for European investors. BIT describes BBIT as currently Europe’s only spot bitcoin ETF.

How investors can access it

BBIT trades in both Swiss francs and US dollars, with Flow Traders acting as market maker. It tracks the SIX Reference Rate Bitcoin Index, and the minimum investment is one unit.

The fund carries a total expense ratio of 0.19% a year, BIT said. Eligible investors can also subscribe in kind by contributing bitcoin directly, subject to the prospectus.

Its public offering is limited to Switzerland, and it is not available to US persons. BIT said it can be bought via banks, brokers and investment platforms with SIX access, without a digital wallet or crypto exchange account.

The Block reported that BIT pointed to investors outside the US, including Asian clients of Swiss private banks, as a potential audience. It did not specify which investors outside Switzerland could buy the fund.

“If investors want a US product, they have plenty of choice. If they want a non-US product in a neutral jurisdiction, until now they really didn’t,” said Cynthia Wu, co-founder and chief commercial officer of BIT.

Launch into a weak market

The listing comes during a difficult period for bitcoin. US spot bitcoin ETFs recorded about $4.94 billion of net outflows in November through November 24, according to SoSoValue data cited by The Block.

FINMA has warned that bitcoin investments remain highly risky even through an approved ETF. It said providers must give clear risk warnings and pay close attention to suitability under the Financial Services Act (FinSA).

For investors who prefer direct ownership, Invezz’s guide on how to buy bitcoin compares the main routes.

With the listing, the number of ETF issuers on SIX Swiss Exchange rises to 41. The exchange said it has added 325 new ETF listings so far this year.

data.title: Why the recent market rebound may only be temporary
data.description:
US stocks have experienced a meaningful rebound in recent sessions as buyers returned to names that had given them the most trouble.

Nasdaq 100 is up significantly at writing versus its low early on Nov. 25. The bounce demonstrated that investors remain willing to aggressively load up on AI stocks after a steep decline.

But the sustainability of the latest surge depends on whether artificial intelligence companies can turn their spending on chips and data centers into enough profit to justify premium multiples.

And recent research gives investors reason to question how much they are paying.

A sharp bounce can leave most of the damage intact

Nvidia gained 4.7% in Friday’s premarket, but its last closing price was still more than 37% below its October record. A stock down that far needs to rise roughly 60% just to get back to its old high.

That gap helps explain how a rally can look dramatic on a trading screen while leaving the broader selloff largely intact.

The S&P 500 and Nasdaq were still on course for their worst November since 2008, even as both headed for their best week since August.

“The questions that caused the market panic are still unanswered,” XTB research director Kathleen Brooks told Reuters.

Friday’s shortened session could also mean lighter trading, leaving the rebound to face a fuller test next week.

The bubble study’s most telling finding goes beyond 97%

Researchers at “London Business School” and the “University of Cambridge” used nearly 796,000 articles from The Economist to build a gauge of speculative excess.

One model put the odds that AI shares were in a bubble at 97%, while two others put them near 40%.

The wide gap shows how much the estimate depends on the model. The finding that matters more for the rebound is what happened after the gauge rose historically.

Nasdaq returns tended to be weaker over the following year, even after accounting for valuations.

That leaves room for sharp rallies along the way. But it also suggests that shares can look cheap compared with their October highs while still offering disappointing returns from here.

The next test is whether AI spending pays for itself

A data center can be valuable to customers while delivering a thin return to the company that paid to build it.

The amounts that cloud providers spend on chips, electricity and financing will matter alongside how much customers actually pay for AI services.

If usage grows but providers have to cut prices to fill capacity, revenue can climb while profit margins shrink.

Borrowing adds pressure, especially with traders already pricing in a December Federal Reserve rate hike. That makes the next round of earnings a more consequential test than Friday’s rebound.

Investors will get to see whether the companies committing billions to AI are generating enough cash from it to support that spending.

data.title: Micron stock is highly undervalued as the Wyckoff Theory takes shape
data.description:
Micron stock has slipped into a bear market this month and now appears to be in the Wyckoff theory's markdown phase, even as its key valuation metric has fallen to bargain levels. MU was trading at $601, about 52% below its year-high. So, is this a good time to buy the dip, or should investors sell the rip?

Micron stock has become highly undervalued

In theory, companies that are seeing substantial revenue and profit growth should receive premium valuations. Some of the most popular companies that have always had a premium valuation are Walmart, Costco, and Shopify. 

Micron, however, is doing the opposite. Its revenue growth is soaring, and analysts expect the momentum will continue. The most recent results showed that its fourth-quarter revenue jumped by 379% to $54.2 billion, with its annual figure hitting $133.2 billion. Most of this growth was in its DRAM division, which made $39.8 billion. 

Micron is also a highly profitable company, with the gross margin of all its businesses being over 80%. Its total gross profit margin rose to 87%, much higher than most companies, including Nvidia. 

Most importantly, analysts believe that the company has more room for growth. For example, the first-quarter revenue is expected to hit $61 billion, while the second-quarter figure will soar to $66 billion. Its annual revenue is expected to jump by 106% to $275 billion. 

For a company experiencing this growth, its valuation metrics are significantly low. For example, the forward price-to-earnings ratio stands at just 3.43, much lower than the sector median of 18. 

Similarly, the company has one of the highest rule-of-40 metrics. This multiple is calculated by adding its revenue growth and its profit margins. Micron has a forward revenue growth of 106% and a profit margin of 64%, giving it a multiple of 170%. 

These metrics explain why the company is planning to accelerate its share repurchases in the near term. Its plan is to start a $35 billion program in December when the buyback restrictions end. Share buybacks help to boost a company’s earnings per share by reducing its outstanding shares.

Micron is facing risks

Therefore, the falling Micron stock price and cheaper valuation is happening because of the rising risks in the industry. One of the main risks is that the AI bubble may burst soon. The AI Stock Bubble Index has remained above 60.

There are also concerns that some AI data center companies will find it hard to survive as financing in the industry dries out. Elon Musk has warned that over 200 neocloud companies will collapse.

These fears have risen after the recent Anthropic IPO, in which the company raised over $100 billion. Its stock has plunged afterwards. OpenAI has also struggled in its fundraising. It recently raised $11 billion, much lower the $30 billion it was aiming for. 

There is also a risk that the memory supercycle will end in the coming months or years. Historically, this business is usually made up of major boom-and-bust cycles.

READ MORE: Micron, SanDisk continue their bloodbath; how long will the pain continue?

Micron share price is in the markdown phase

MU stock chart | Source: TradingView

The weekly chart shows that MU stock has formed the classic Wyckoff Method. It remained in a consolidation phase for years, a sign that it was in the accumulation phase. 

The stock then entered the markup phase mid-last year and then started its upward trend, eventually reaching a record high of $1,255. Now, there are signs that it has dropped into the markdown phase, which is characterized by panic selling.

Therefore, the stock will likely continue falling in the near term. The next key level to watch will be at the 50-week moving average of $523.

data.title: CMC Markets profit more than doubles to £106M on record first half
data.description:
CMC Markets has reported a record first half, with pre-tax profit more than doubling as its business-to-business (B2B) and institutional arms offset subdued market volatility.

The London-listed broker said profit before tax rose 115% to £106.0 million in the six months to September 30, 2026, from £49.3 million a year earlier, according to its interim results published on November 26, 2026.

Net operating income climbed 54% to £286.6 million, from £186.2 million. CMC said that beat its previous first-half record of £230.9 million, set in HY2021.

Trading revenue leads the gains

Net trading revenue rose 67% to £230.9 million and now makes up about 81% of group income, up from 74%, the company said. The institutional channel showed the fastest growth.

CMC said the record came even though the VIX volatility index stayed below its historical average for most of the period, unlike the more volatile first half of the previous year.

Net investing revenue increased 8% to £28.3 million, while net interest income rose 28% to £25.6 million, helped by active management of group and client cash.

Its Australian stockbroking business posted another record half, with net operating income up 5% to A$69.2 million.

Costs rise more slowly than income

Operating expenses rose 31% to £177.6 million, reflecting higher variable pay, expansion and technology spending, CMC said. Excluding variable remuneration, costs were £152.5 million, up from £128.4 million.

That lifted the pre-tax margin to 37.0% from 26.5%. EBITDA more than doubled to £116.5 million, and basic earnings per share rose to 29.0p from 13.3p.

The board declared a record interim dividend of 10.1p a share, up 84% from 5.5p.

CMC also completed its first £250 million Euro Medium Term Note (EMTN) issue in August, which it said was significantly oversubscribed.

Big partnerships still to come

The broker reiterated its upgraded FY2027 guidance of net operating income of at least £550 million and EBITDA of £250 million. Its financial year ends in March.

CMC said its Westpac stockbroking deal is now expected to launch in the first half of FY2028. Once live, it is expected to be the group’s largest partnership of its kind.

Staff accounts for the ASB partnership in New Zealand are live for end-to-end testing, with launch expected imminently. CMC has also expanded a deal with an unnamed neobank to provide liquidity for CFDs and other derivatives in the UK.

Dubai, warrants and crypto

CMC said its Dubai business doubled revenue between FY2025 and FY2026 and is now its fourth global hub, alongside the UK, Australia and Singapore. It has applied for expanded regulatory permissions there.

Its European warrants business has issued about 8,000 products. CMC plans an Australian warrants pilot trade before the end of 2026, having signed agreements with ASX, BNP Paribas and others.

After the period end, CMC was approved by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) as a cryptoasset business under the UK’s Money Laundering Regulations, the results statement said.

The broker has also added fractional investing, 24/5 trading in US equities and global indices, and wider options coverage to its trading platform.

“Achieving this performance against exceptionally subdued market volatility is particularly significant,” chief executive Lord Cruddas said.

“It demonstrates how far we have moved beyond a business whose performance is principally driven by the retail trading cycle,” he added. Cruddas said his recent personal share purchases of about £5 million “should underline that confidence to the market”.

CMC’s next scheduled update is its FY2027 results in June 2027.

data.title: AMD, Intel, Broadcom rally in premarket trading Friday as AI stocks rebound
data.description:
Chip stocks were rallying in premarket trading on Friday as investors bought the dip following the Thanksgiving holiday.

Intel and AMD gained roughly 4% and Broadcom jumped 3% in early premarket trading at 6:45 AM ET.

All three stocks, alongside major names in the artificial intelligence trade, have been under pressure in recent weeks, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq briefly entering bear-market territory in the previous session.

Intel had shed 0.6% on Wednesday to close at $54.47, AMD had lost 1.75% to $406 while Broadcom stayed almost flat at $300.86.

The broader market was also looking set to jump, with futures linked to all three major indexes rising ahead of the shortened trading session to close the week.

However, with fundamental questions around the sustainability of the AI trade still looming, analysts are unsure whether the rebound will be durable.

"The recovery in stocks seems technical. The questions that caused the market panic are still unanswered," Kathleen Brooks, research director at XTB, told Reuters. "If these gains can be sustained on Friday, it would suggest that enthusiasm for the AI trade is back."

There have nevertheless been some positive developments for individual chipmakers that could help support sentiment.

Intel gets two important customer wins

Intel has secured two important customer developments that could support its manufacturing ambitions.

CEO Lip-Bu Tan announced Thursday that the company had signed its first external customer for its advanced 18A-P chip manufacturing process.

Intel has not disclosed the customer's identity, but the agreement marks progress in its effort to compete with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co.

Separately, Microsoft became the first publicly named customer for Intel Foundry's EMIB advanced packaging technology, which will be used for Microsoft's Azure first-party silicon.

AMD jumps from Hunterbrook-triggered selloff

AMD has also made progress in its efforts to secure a larger share of the AI infrastructure market even as it struggles with allegations of links with blacklisted Chinese firms.

On November 16, AI infrastructure provider TensorWave announced a six-year agreement with OpenAI to supply 457 megawatts of dedicated computing capacity across multiple US data-center locations.

AMD has also completed its acquisitions of AI research startup World Labs, led by Fei-Fei Li, and specialised inference-chip developer Taalas.

China’s extension of the pause in controls on critical minerals till January is another good news for chipmakers, even though it is only a short-term relief.

Minerals like gallium and germanium are critical inputs in semiconductor manufacturing.

Analysts also remain bullish on the stock with TipRanks data showing 27 out of 30 analysts keeping a 'buy' rating and three suggesting 'hold'.

Broadcom has a major Anthropic deal

Broadcom has also faced significant pressure recently and investors chipped in on Friday to buy the stock, pushing it up before the opening bell.

It recently secured a significant development in its AI business through a financing arrangement involving some of Wall Street's biggest financial institutions.

Bank of America, Blackstone, Citi and Morgan Stanley announced a $63 billion financing structure in October to fund the purchase of Broadcom's custom AI accelerators and networking equipment for Anthropic.

Several Wall Street firms, including StoneX, UBS, and Rosenblatt have reiterated their Buy ratings on Broadcom, but some like Rothschild Redburn have also downgraded the stock with concerns over AI financing and the sustainability of earnings.

Broadcom is scheduled to report its fourth-quarter and full-year 2026 financial results on December 9, giving investors another opportunity to assess whether its AI business can sustain growth despite recent concerns about chip demand.
